Messages.Author: John Whelan
Messages.Body:
librarian wrote:
> Well, but if it's Lasombra, Nos, Trem, and !Ventrue, do we need more
> vamps from those clans (sure, they would be great, but some people are
> keeping track of which clans have what vamps in which groups - won't new
> one's throw that out of whack?).

Depends on the group they are coming from. Groups 3+4 seem
essentially complete, with each Camarilla clan having 26 to 29 members
in Groups 3+4 (not counting multiple versions of the same vamp via the
advanced rule). With 28 members, the Tremere are already fairly
numerous. the Nosferatu have 29 members in 3+4.

Most Sabbat clans have only 23 members in Group 3-4 (with some
variation). The Lasombra have a full complement with 23. The !
Ventrue still have only 22.

There is, however, room to add vampires to Group 5. The clans listed
(Las Nos, Trem, !Ven) are about 4 to 7 members behind a full
complement. Giving each clan new vamps would temporarily put them
ahead for a little while ... until the next expansion.

Messages.Author: Jussi Hattara
Messages.Body:


Quick stats extracted from the Secret Library from the groupings

Lasombra: 2+3: 23 / 3+4: 23 / 4+5: 17
Nosferatu: 1+2: 24 / 2+3: 26 / 3+4: 30 / 4+5: 21
Tremere: 1+2: 25 / 2+3: 27 / 3+4: 28 / 4+5: 22
Ventrue antitribu: 2+3: 23 / 3+4: 22 / 4+5: 16

So all of the base clans have at least 3 slots left for group 5, no
matter how you count, but their group 4 is pretty much full.

Then let's take a look at the corresponding bloodlines

Gargoyle: 2+3: 9 / 3+4: 3 / 4+5: 2 (plenty of room in group 4)
Kiasyd: 2+3: 6 / 3+4: 5 / 4+5: 4 (1 more to group 4, 1 for group 5)
Salubri antitribu: 2+3: 6 / 3+4: 5 / 4+5: 4 (1 more to group 4, 1 for
group 5)
Samedi: 2+3: 7 / 3+4: 5 / 4+5: 4 (1 more to group 4, 1 for group 5)

Pretty much the same situation with all the other bloodlines across
the board (exceptions are Gargoyles and Blood Brothers with less
vampires and Baali with groups 4 and 5 filled).

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
Jussi Hattara <jhat...@tenerdo.org> wrote:
>Then let's take a look at the corresponding bloodlines

>Salubri antitribu: 2+3: 6 / 3+4: 5 / 4+5: 4 (1 more to group 4, 1 for
>group 5)
>Samedi: 2+3: 7 / 3+4: 5 / 4+5: 4 (1 more to group 4, 1 for group 5)
>
>Pretty much the same situation with all the other bloodlines across
>the board (exceptions are Gargoyles and Blood Brothers with less
>vampires and Baali with groups 4 and 5 filled).

One option here is to add an Advanced vampire or two. There are very
few such vampires for the Bloodlines. Because of the inherent
limitations on Advanced vampires (such as not being able to bring out
both, separately), they don't seem to count as a wholly separate
vampire.

It's also possible that some of the vampires in the starter might be
reprints of key vampires from the previous group. It would be perfectly
feasible, for example, to have a starter that went:

- 1 x reprint Lasombra A - say, Lucy Markowitz
- 1 x reprint Lasbomra B - say, Virginie or Ermenegildo
- 1 x reprint Kiasyd C - say, Dame Hollerton
- 1 x reprint Kiasyd D - say, Omme Enberbenight
- 2 x new Lasombra E (group 5)
- 2 x new Advanced Kiasyd - say, an 8 cap Omme
- 2 x new Kiasyd F
- 2 x new Kiasyd G

So you get twice as many Kiasyd cards as Lasombra. A brand new player
has four-and-a-half Kiasyd to mix and match with, and 3 different
Lasombra to play with. Existing players can get 4 copies of all the new
vampires with only 2 starter purchases - so there's flexibility, without
too much gouging.

Then the other 'starter exclusive' cards would be library cards.

Also, LSJ has previously indicated that he'd quite like the group pairs
to be a bit smoother, so we might well see 2 vampires in group 5 rather
than 1 in 4, 1 in 5. So in the above example, F and G might both be
group 5.

Messages.Author: Malone
Messages.Body:
On Sep 7, 10:50 pm, John Whelan <jwjbwhe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> On Sep 2, 4:58 pm, James Coupe <ja...@zephyr.org.uk> wrote:

> > previous examples of 150 (50 of each rarity - presumably two of each on

>
> Could be 50 each of Rare, Uncommon, Common +20 vampires.

That would be problematic. What would the booster distribution be?
Does everyone end up with like 15 copies of each vampire in order to
get enough of everything else, or do you only put one vampire in each
booster?

Since grouping was established, vampires are the one card type that
can be printed freely without risk of upsetting the power curve (or
the overcompensation to that risk, more wallpaper). If anything,
crypt cards should make up more than 1/3 of each set, not less.

I see no problem with the latter solution. (Neither would I be averse
to 19-card boosters, like in the good old days).

> Since grouping was established, vampires are the one card type that
> can be printed freely without risk of upsetting the power curve (or
> the overcompensation to that risk, more wallpaper).  If anything,
> crypt cards should make up more than 1/3 of each set, not less.

Sorry. I don't agree at all. I have no objection to them taking it
slowly and cautiously when creating new sets and new cards, to ensure
balance, but have no desire to have them keep churning out new groups
just because they can.

Anything that adds something new to the game will risk upsetting the
power curve to some extent. The whole point of an expansion is to add
something new to the game.
